hypotheses.justification: The proof never uses hS. barX p X K is defined as (K.subgroupOf X).map (QuotientGroup.mk' (GLAPPrimeCore p X)), so it already intersects K with X. The proof only uses mem_barX_iff, mem_Zc and mem_barCenterX_iff, and none of these needs S ≤ X. Zc S = S ⊓ centralizer S is an arbitrary subgroup of G, and the argument works elementwise. A z ∈ Zc S that lies in X gives the element ⟨z, _⟩ of ↥X. In the proof as written, that membership is supplied by mem_barX_iff applied to hζ. The statement is therefore true and the same proof compiles with hS deleted. hS is mentioned only by this binder, and no other part of the statement depends on it.

This is a section variable, taken as an argument because it is instance-implicit and G is already an argument. Nothing in the statement needs it: barX is defined in GammaStarConj.lean with only [Group G], barCenterX in Sec6DInputs.lean with only [Group G], and Zc in Sec6DHeis.lean with only a group. GLAPPrimeCore is defined for any group. The only place Finite G enters the proof is through the lemma mem_barCenterX_iff, which picks up the section variable [Finite G] although its proof does not use it. Its proof just unfolds barCenterX with Subgroup.mem_map and Subgroup.mem_center_iff. So the theorem holds for arbitrary groups. A proof without Finite G can inline that unfolding, or the lemma can be given `omit [Finite G] in`. This is independent of hS, and both can be deleted together.
